text:
maria: quick heads-up — the sample-app observability probe is showing a mismatch between the SDK's request id and our app logs. i can repro locally.

maria: steps: start sample-app, make a request to /generate, look at stdout and the SDK debug log.

maria: SDK snippet i'm using:
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=env['REDWOOD_KEY'])
resp = client.generate('hello')
```

maria: logs (truncated):
```
2024-03-12T12:23:01Z app INFO request_id=app-9a2c gen started
2024-03-12T12:23:01Z sdk DEBUG x-request-id=sdk-3f4b sending request
2024-03-12T12:23:02Z app INFO request_id=app-9a2c gen finished
```

maria: expected the SDK to surface the same request id (or at least correlate). looks like SDK sends `x-request-id: sdk-3f4b` but our logging middleware reads `request_id` from contextvar.

jon: thanks for the repro, maria. this smells like a header-to-context handoff gap when using the py sdk + fastapi sample.

jon: quick notes: the SDK currently injects `X-Request-Id` for outgoing calls (so the server sees it), but the sample-app's logging middleware expects `X-Log-Id` (custom) or populates its own contextvar from incoming headers. so two things can diverge: header name mismatch and async background tasks losing the contextvar.

ingrid: fwiw we see this most when the request is proxied through the async worker pool (uvicorn -> background task). contextvars don't cross TaskGroup/ThreadPool boundaries automatically.

sam: idea: add an observation hook in the SDK to explicitly set the `redwood.log_id` contextvar on call start if a header is present in the response, and also allow configuring the header name to read (default `X-Request-Id`). would that help?

maria: yes that would. short-term i hacked the sample-app logging middleware to accept `X-Request-Id` as well and it lined up. long-term a configurable binding makes sense.

jon: implementation sketch:
```py
# in sdk/http.py
async def _on_response(resp):
    header = resp.headers.get(config.log_id_header, None)
    if header:
        # propagate into our logging context for the app runtime
        try:
            import contextvars
            LOG_ID.set(header)
        except Exception:
            pass
```
jon: plus an option on client init: `log_id_header='X-Request-Id'` and `propagate_log_id=True`. keep it opt-in so we don't interfere with apps that expect their own ids.

ingrid: also add docs calling out async caveat: when using background tasks you may need `contextvars.copy_context()` or to set log id inside the task. we should add a sample snippet for FastAPI BackgroundTasks.

sam: question for maintainers: should this hook run for inbound responses only (when SDK is client to our hosted infra) or also for outgoing requests (when SDK used inside Redwood private deployments)?

jon: run-for-responses only — we only want to harvest server-generated ids to correlate. For outgoing requests (SDK -> user service) we should continue to set `X-Request-Id` but not override app context.

maria: can we also expose a lightweight sync fallback? some sample apps are sync-only.

jon: yes — same logic in sync path. add tests for both httpx async and requests sync adapters.

sam: i'll open a small RFC PR with the config keys and tests. tagging @ingrid for the docs snippet.

ingrid: ack — i'll add a FastAPI sample showing how to consume `X-Request-Id` from incoming requests and how to forward it into background tasks.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy for `devex/sdk-logid-probe` scheduled at 2024-03-13T04:00Z :rocket:

maria: thanks all — this should unblock the sample-app onboarding notes. i'll link the temporary hack change in the sample repo and follow up once the SDK PR lands. :clap:
